Question: What is your review of Mrs. Serial Killer (Netflix India Film)?
Old_Answer: Mrs. Serial Killer is what happens when uncreative people with no knowledge of screenplay, direction and dialogues have money to spend and assume they can entertain people. What was Netflix thinking about when they took up distribution for it? Perhaps they were fooled like most of us by the trailers during the lockdown. The director is Sirish Kunder. If you do not know him, let me remind you the movies he has been associated with. Joker (the Hindi one with Akshay Kumar) Tees Maar Khan Jaan-E-Mann Along with wife Farah Khan, they set out to waste my 1 hour and 46 minutes imagining a thriller straight out of Hollywood that literally has no plot twists. The movie is like asking a child, “What is 2 + 2?” Unless the child is dumb, he will reply 4. That is the case with this movie. It is predictable and you have to be extremely dumb to think otherwise. The Good: Manoj Bajpai’s screen presence is short-lived and even he could not save the story which has more plotholes than potholes on Bangalore streets. He is the only good thing about this movie, other than Mohit Raina. The Bad: Action: They could have done so well with the limited action scenes that they had to direct but they messed it all up. Slow motion falls, ninja kicks and Spider-man on the wall right in the middle of a thriller does not really gel up together. They created an entire valley of flowers with VFX in the middle of nowhere just to intoxicate a victim. Even that scene seemed copied straight out of a Korean movie. Acting: Jacqueline Fernandez is not an apt choice to play a female serial killer. The accent coupled with her non-existential screen presence just does not help. There are a ton of actors who could have played the role in a better manner. I guess, the director knew the film is not up to the mark, and sought in some glamour to lure the audience. There are two other recurring characters other than the mentioned above, and it seems they were hired because they worked just for free food and to get a selfie with Jacqueline. Direction & Screenplay: Well, it is all over the place. When your try to show the future before showing the past, you justify it through the story but nothing of that sort happens. Jacqueline suddenly turns into this psycho killer and suddenly not, there is no cause to it. Even though the color palettes were used wonderfully in some scenes, it is totally destroyed by the direction in the scenes. Climax: I assume they ran out of story and they had promised Netflix that they will make a movie close to two hours. Hence, they just stretched the climax for so long that I had to literally fast forward because I already knew what was about to happen. Thriller movies do not have such long climaxes with absurd direction and predictability. It was so boring I has already started seeing recommendations for my next watch. Ending: The most heinous ending. Movies have a purpose and morale to them. This movie sets one all along, then changes it and then changes it again in a stupid manner only to make you feel it was a cleverly written thriller from the beginning. Loopholes: I counted at least 5 of them but lets not make this review any longer by discussing them. It is a solid 1 out of 5 for me. Do not watch it! Try these movies on Netflix instead! And for heaven’s sake, someone please ask Sirish Kunder and family to stop making movies.

Perhaps, I will never tell you whatever I wrote and I know perhaps you may never even read this but this is what love is to me. Not expecting anything from you and yet dying to get a glimpse just once every day. This is what love is for me, no boundaries, no limitations, me writing poems for you, you knowing that I exist and me being grateful to my stars that I can see you, know you and be this weirdly awkward shy guy that I am.
